question: Does satisfying a traffic signal warrant automatically require installation of a traffic control signal?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. Meeting one or more traffic signal warrants does not by itself require installing a traffic control signal — this is an explicit mandatory provision. Warrant satisfaction is only one factor in an engineering study, and the MUTCD even recommends considering alternatives to signals when warrants are met, since signals can sometimes increase delay or certain crash types. A parallel rule applies to all-way stop control warrants. Standards (mandatory): - "The satisfaction of a traffic signal warrant or warrants shall not in itself require the installation of a traffic control signal." - "The satisfaction of an all-way stop control warrant or warrants shall not in itself require the installation of all-way stop control at an unsignalized intersection." Guidance (recommended): - Because road user delay and the frequency of some types of crashes are sometimes higher under signal control than under STOP sign control, consideration should be given to providing alternatives to traffic control signals even if one or more signal warrants has been satisfied. - Where volumes must be projected (e.g., locations under development or construction), hourly volumes should be estimated as part of an engineering study for comparison with warrants; except where Warrant 8 is the justification, a signal installed under projected conditions should have an engineering study done within 1 year of steady (stop-and-go) operation to determine if it is justified — if not, it should be taken out of steady operation or removed. Citations: - Section 4C.01 Standard §3 (p.651) - Section 2B.12 Standard §5 (p.79) - Section 4B.03 Guidance §1 (p.649) - Section 4C.01 Guidance §12 (p.652) - Section 4C.01 Support §20 (p.653) - Section 4C.08 Support §1 (p.661)
gold_answer: No. A warrant is a threshold that triggers analysis; it is not conclusive justification. Installation must be based on an engineering study considering safety, operation, alternatives, and the site. A signal can also be installed where no warrant is met if an engineering study documents why it is the best solution.
